📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What if you make this the year you don't fill all the stockings with candy or gift cards? Both have their place, but if you want to make this the best Christmas ever, you have to shove some tech in those stockings. The good news: Tech gifts don’t have to be expensive to be impressive.

According to recent reports, no matter who you're shopping for, there are tons of affordable gizmos that are some combination of cool and useful and that feel pricier than they are. Here are 20 cool tech stocking stuffers to light up any holiday morning, all of which cost less than $50.

Industry observers note that if there's an old-school gamer on your list, their Christmas morning will be extra merry if it includes a tiny video game emulator. R36T Retro Gaming Console ($48.98) puts over 18,000 video games in the palm of your hand. It has a 3.5" screen, so whether they like arcade classics or consoles-of-the-past, they can fit 'em all in a pocket.

The Xteink X4 is an e-reader that's smaller than your phone. It uses e-ink like an Amazon Kindle, so you can whip a glare-free screen out of your pocket and start reading anywhere there's a light source. The X4 is a no-frills gadget—there's no lighting, touchscreen, or apps—but if you want a cheap, convenient way to read for around $50, it's perfect.

Those disposable cans of compressed air with the red straws are so 2015. Blow the dust off your electronics with an SDFM Electric Air Duster instead. With an engine that moves at 150,000 RPM, it shoots air such high speeds, the dust doesn't stand a chance. It's also cordless and comes with a variety of cleaning attachments to keep your gear in top shape.

If your giftee likes to listen to music or podcasts while drifting off to sleep, the only gift better than a pair of sleep headphones is two pairs of sleep headphones! This two-pack retails for $22.99 and contains two headbands with built in speakers you can pair with your phone or other device easily.

Industry observers note that your giftee may have the tech side of their battle station/home office locked down, but I bet they don't have the aesthetics dialed in. Govee Smart LED Light Bars ($54.99, but at the moment on sale for $34.99) are programmable, colorful light bars that work with Alexa and Google Assistant and can display light effects created from 16 millions colors. It even syncs with your music to provide trippy visuals.

Sources indicate that my lifestyle doesn't involve cutting down trees, but I still need one of these miniature chainsaws. I mean, it's a chainsaw, and it's only six inches long. This Seeii mini chainsaw ($49.99) is battery-powered, so no one will be accidentally cutting the cord. According to the listing, it's suitable for tree pruning, garden artistry, shrub trimming, forest logging, and wood cutting.

You know what computer fiends are missing in their lives? Knobs. This little $33 gadget lets you assign functions to four external knobs and 12 push buttons, so you can finally have a decent volume control, scrub through video smoothly, skip music tracks with a button push, and control any other function easily and physically. Perfect for gamers.

In a recent development, you could use a tape measure like a caveman, or you could measure things with a frickin' laser that fits in your pocket. This $40 gadget has an LED screen that's easy to read and it doubles as a cat toy. But does it measure things? Damn right it measures things—major things, little things, middle-sized things—it doesn't care what you put in front of it, it will measure the hell out of it! (Up to 98 feet, anyway.).

It has been revealed that this compact Bluetooth speaker has an Amazon rating of 4.6 stars out of 5, and it's cheap—just $45. It's waterproof, it sounds great, and it features a built-in light show with six different settings so you can check out cool visuals with your tunes.

Recent findings suggest that A single Apple Airtag makes a great gift to accompany the main gift you don't want someone to lose. Or they can put it on their wallet or your keys, and if they misplace them, they can hit a button and it will play a sound while the FindMy app displays a map that leads to the missing item. Plus, it works in reverse, so you can hit a tag and it will ring your lost phone.

In a recent development, if you want to give the gift of warmth for the holidays, you could do a lot worse than this portable neck, shoulder, and back warmer. There are three temperature settings, a safety shut-off feature, and it heats up really fast, for only $33.

This tiny little vacuum from Odistar will keep their desktop dust-free. It sucks with 1000Pa of suction power for 400 minutes off a single charge, and it's very easy to use: You put it in the palm of your hand and push it around. Cool!

Industry observers note that it's not like people need an endoscope camera every day, but if the need for a tiny camera does arise—if they need to see why the engine isn't working or if their wedding ring falls behind the oven—they'll be glad to have this Anykit USB Endoscope Camera. It plugs right into an Android or iPhone and captures HD photos and video of places the sun don't shine.

Sources indicate that if your giftee is carrying their laptop around to coffeehouses like a chump, this is the perfect present. They can connect a foldable mini Bluetooth keyboard from iClever to their phone, and turn it into an ultra-portable productivity device. It even has a little trackpad!

This skinny extra battery charges a phone magnetically or with a USB-C cable. It's fast, too. It can charge an iPhone 16 Pro Max to 37% in 30 minutes via the USB-C port and it's less than three inches wide.

Projectors have gotten really good and really small over the last few years, and they prices have come down massively too. This mini projector costs only $29 and projects a 720p image up to 120" and it weighs only about two pounds.

It has been revealed that most people already have a media streamer attached to their televisions, but in case you're gifting someone who doesn't, the Roku Streaming Stick 4K is a solid choice in the $50 price range. This no-frills device serves up 4K HD video, gives you access to hundreds of free and premium channels, and is easy to setup.

It has been revealed that the Twelve South AirFly SE is an ultra-compact Bluetooth transmitter lets you plug into any device with a 3.5 mm jack, like in-flight entertainment systems, gym machines, or TVs, and stream audio wirelessly to your Bluetooth earbuds or headphones. Leave those accursed wired headphone in the drawer where they belong!

In a recent development, this is an essential gift if there's a cyclist in your life and anyone who wants to maintain proper PSI in their car tires. This portable air compressor weighs less than a pound and is a steal at only $40. It's rechargeable, has an onboard pressure gauge, an LED flashlight, and can inflate a car tire in only eight minutes.

I am 100% sure anyone you give this to will be able to use it. This compact, high‑power Anker charger has two USB‑C ports plus one USB‑A, letting you power up your laptop, phone, and tablet all at once, from one plug. Plus it charges fast.

In a recent development, sonos is one of the best-known names in multi-room audio, but its collection of speakers, soundbars, headphones and subwoofers doesn't come cheap. I've been using Sonos products in my own house for over a decade, and I always wait until Black Friday to upgrade to my system.

One of my favorite combos is using the excellent Sonos Ace headphones with my Beam soundbar to swap between room-filling audio and private listening with the TV Swap feature. The Sonos Ace are now just $229 at Amazon, which is the lowest price they've ever been. And a Beam Gen 2 soundbar is down 39% to $339 right now!

I know Sonos has (rightly) taken a battering for app mistakes in recent years but what I love about it is that you can take opportunities like Black Friday to build out your system without necessarily having to chuck away what you replace. Personally, I'm eyeing up the Sonos Move 2, which is $100 off — and it'll mean my current Sonos Move (Gen 1) can be relocated to the garage.

Here are the best Sonos deals I've seen (so far) for both the U.S. and the U.K., and I'll make sure to enhancement this page with any new deals I spot as we get closer to Black Friday itself.

The Sonos Ace were the first over-ear headphones from Sonos and a pretty darn good attempt, too. They've since been replaced by a successor but that means the original model has dropped down to its lowest ever price. You get big, airy sound and some very good spatial tuning. The 30 hours of battery is a big bonus, and it helped them earn a 4.5-star review on launch. This is their lowest price ever and they're the same headphones I use myself most days.

The Beam Gen 2 is a step up from the Beam Gen 1 I use in my house and despite its small footprint, it can easily fill a room with sound. Check out our 4-star review to see why we rate this bar so highly. As discussed, you can build out a Sonos system so the Beam Gen 2 can connect to the sub and Era 100 elsewhere on this list for extra surround and extra bass.

In a recent development, the Sonos Arc Ultra is a wicked soundbar with incredible Dolby Atmos for your movies. If you want the best bass you'll want to add some form of subwoofer (the Sub 4 or Sub mini), but then you've got one of the best "out of box" home theater setups around.

Industry observers note that this Sub Mini deal is a solid $100 off, although the starting price has been hiked since last year, so while it's a discount, it's not the biggest saving it could possibly be. However, the product itself is excellent (I own one of these) and it's surprisingly powerful for something so compact. You'll get the extra rumbles and shakes in your movies and it'll fill out the low end in your music. Looks pretty slick, too — especially in white.

It has been revealed that the Sonos Era 100 is a happy, flexible little smart speaker, with great sound quality, no matter where you put it. We gave it 4.5 stars in our review, thanks to its excellent sound quality and compact size. This deal isn't quite the lowest we've seen on the speaker, but it's a solid saving nonetheless.

In a recent development, the Sonos Move 2 packs some serious upgrades with a battery life boost to 24 hours for all-day listening on the move (up from 10 hours on the original Move) as well as simultaneous Bluetooth and Wi-Fi pairing. It looks identical to the original Move except that it's also available in an olive colorway.

Industry observers note that this little smart speaker is compact and versatile. I have the original Roam and it will connect to your Wi-Fi at home and then swap to Bluetooth when you're out and about. There are 10 hours of playback from a full charge — don't use it all up at once!

Industry observers note that this is a rich-sounding soundbar for something so small. It's the perfect audio center for a small room, giving out loads of sound without taking up much space. One thing I like about it is, even before the discount, it's a solid budget option. Not everything Sonos makes has to be a wallet-crusher.

This compact soundbar supports Dolby Atmos for a wider soundstage when you're watching movies. You can even connect other Sonos speakers to it to act as a physical surround — a mini home cinema, just for you. As well as being reduced in the U.S., British readers can nab a discount on this bar, too.

If you want some extra bass to go with your Sonos system but don't want something as significant and impressive as the Sub 4, then the Sub mini is the way to go. It provides a lovely meaty kick to your movies and enriches the sound of your TV shows.

In a recent development, the Sonos Era 300 is a mighty wireless speaker, providing Dolby Atmos listening to compatible tracks. It sounds incredibly rich, and you can connect two of them together (if you're feeling flush) for a stereo sound that beats the heck out of similarly priced options.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CAD images of the iPhone 18e, said to come from a previously reliable source, have shown a rather odd new design for the camera bump.

If accurate, it would represent a big change from its predecessor, which simply has a single lens protruding without a surrounding bump or plateau ….

Sources indicate that the iPhone 17e was launched in March with a design unchanged from last year’s iPhone 16e. While the camera did get some feature enhancements, including the ability to store depth information for portrait photos, the physical camera design remained the same.

The current model has a single lens protruding directly from the casing with a flush-mounted flashlight next to it. Engadget reports on CAD images showing a very different approach with next year’s iPhone 18e.

The renders show an almost square camera bump measuring about 28 mm by 35 mm that houses the single rear camera, the LED flash and the rear microphone.

The site doesn’t share the images, but says that the camera bump looks similar to that of the M5 iPad Pro, shown below.

It’s unclear what might have prompted the change of design, especially as the site’s Filipe Espósito claims he’s also seen CAD models for the standard model iPhone 18 or the iPhone Air 2, neither of which adopt it.

Previous reports have suggested that the only spec change with the iPhone 18e over its predecessor will be performance improvements thanks to the A20 chip.

  • Name: Saint-PierreCountry: CanadaProducer: Hawco ProductionsNetwork: CBCDistributor: Fifth SeasonFor fans of: Death in Paradise, Shetland, Lupin Watch on Deadline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that welcome to Global Breakouts, Deadline’s strand in which, each fortnight, we shine a spotlight on the TV indicates and films killing it in their local territories. The industry is as globalized as it’s ever been, but breakout hits are appearing in pockets of the world all the time and it can be hard to keep track… So, we’re going to do the hard work for you.

This week we go north of the American border to hear from the maker and star of breakout Canadian police procedural Saint-Pierre. The show, which sees Allan Hawco playing exiled Royal Newfoundland Constabulary Inspector Donny ‘Fitz’ Fitzpatrick alongside Joséphine Jobert as Deputy Chief Geneviève ‘Arch’ Archambault. Together they investigate crimes across Saint Pierre and Miquelon in the French collectivity in North America. Numeris data highlights it was CBC‘s most popular show in the 2025/26 season and among the most watched across Canada. Related Stories News Design Duo Brian Gluckstein & Lynda Reeves Set Video Podcast With Marlo Miazga's M Media Casting January Jones, Stephen Dorff & Lionel Boyce Among Upcoming Additions To Comedy 'The Family Disappears'.

Name: Saint-PierreCountry: CanadaProducer: Hawco ProductionsNetwork: CBCDistributor: Fifth SeasonFor fans of: Death in Paradise, Shetland, Lupin Watch on Deadline.

Given that Saint-Pierre was CBC’s most-watched drama series of the 2025/26 and we were flagging it as far back as MIPCOM 2024, it should really come as no surprise it’s now featuring as a Global Breakout. What is surprising is that the show hasn’t got a U.S. deal yet.

The show, which stars Allan Hawco as an exiled Canadian police officer reassigned to the French-controlled islands of Saint Pierre and Miquelon in the Atlantic Ocean near Newfoundland, was in 2024 picked up for distribution by Fifth Season, which has shopped it around the world diligently to the likes of U&Alibi in the UK, France Télévisions in France, the ABC in Australia, Sky in Latest Zealand, Disney+ across Eastern Europe and Belgium, Quebecor Content in French Canada and BBC Studios in the Netherlands and Poland among others.

For Hawco, who writes, produces and stars in the show, a deal south of the border is probably just time away.

According to recent reports, “We’re super happy with how it has been performing in Canada – my understanding is we’re among the highest-rated reveals in Canada and among the top-viewed shows on CBC,” he indicates. “We’ve also been doing very well internationally, and it’s only a matter of time before we find the right home in the U.S. market. Our partner Fifth Season leads the way in sales outside Canada, and I know they’ve been very selective about where that home should be.”.

Hawco had the idea for Saint-Pierre, which he co-created with Robina Lord-Stafford, while scouting locations for another CBC show that Hawco Productions co-produces, Son of a Critch. “We were sitting outside on a patio at the end of the day, and the idea hit me like a freight train,” he states. “I saw the entire idea – some of the characters and the bones of the larger idea – but the real stuff happened once CBC were on board, and Robina and I started working together.”.

The result was a mystery-of-the-week format that mixed the cosy crime notes of series such as Death in Paradise with darker themes and grittier storylines. It’s a unique result, and one that CBC audiences have been lapping up.

Hawco’s Fitz – a street smart detective who relies on gut feelings – is exiled to Saint-Pierre after his investigations take him too close to a corrupt politician, while Joséphine Jobert’s Deputy Chief Geneviève ‘Arch’ Archambault is a guarded but super-smart detective with a sarcastic edge. It’s a classic odd couple set up, where Fitz’s freestyle jazz approach to police work rubs up against Arch’s analytical mind. Of course, the two eventually find an unconventional groove.

It has been revealed that but why anchor the series on a sleepy fishing village? “Because it’s awesome. Truly,” responds Hawco. “The entire concept was spawned from being there, and Saint-Pierre inspired our entire world and show. In the end, no matter how many titles we workshopped internally – the name was always going to be Saint-Pierre, as in many ways it’s the lead character and always was.”.

According to recent reports, hawco himself, a veteran actor and producer with credits for the Republic of Doyle and The Book of Negroes among others, shoulders a significant amount of heavy lifting with his on- and off-screen roles “It’s definitely a heavy lift, but I’ve been doing it since Republic of Doyle days,” he says. “Being a co-creator, co-showrunner, executive producer, and lead actor means you never really turn off.

“Fortunately, I have an incredible team. Sharing showrunning duties with Robina Lord-Stafford makes all the difference, and Joséphine Jobert is a phenomenal on-screen partner. The hardest part is the sheer volume of work, especially when we split production between St. John’s and Saint-Pierre, but being involved at every level makes sure the show feels like one cohesive piece. But it takes a village: My producing team is incredible. Our directors are excellent, and the cast makes the days fly faster than I wish they did at times.”.

Canadian TV has been on an upwards trajectory, with streamers investing more locally and the networks continuing to spend. There’s also that little ice hockey drama over at Crave, Heated Rivalry. Even so, getting ideas away remains tough and there’s no doubt the more commercial elements of Saint-Pierre have been part of its popularity at CBC, and long with hard graft in pulling in other cash sources.

“Financing a Canadian show always has its challenges, and the logistical puzzle of making a series like Saint-Pierre brings an even greater level of complexity to the mix,” states Hawco. “Having said that, as a company and as a team at Hawco Productions – we’re uniquely skilled at bringing a lot to the screen with a smaller budget in comparison to demonstrates that may compare in scope and size.

“It’s not as simple as the CBC just writing us a cheque. We have the international component, Ontario and Newfoundland’s labour tax credits – Newfoundland and Labrador’s incentive program is a massive part of our success and ability to shoot here.”.

According to recent reports, the show, Hawco believes, reflects the talent working in Canada. “We are excellent at making great material in this country,” he claims, and now “the world is seeing that.”.

CBC will be hoping for more of the same with the upcoming return of Saint-Pierre. “Season 3 of the show is deep in production, with the likes of new cast members Assaad Bouab and Caroline Dhavernas set to “shake up the dynamic,” says Hawco. “We have plenty of stories left to tell,” he adds.

The audio quality is second to none, with the fully customizable EQ giving you plenty of options to get the sound how you like it. Sources indicate that samsung’s 32-inch Odyssey G5 (G51F) gaming monitor has dropped to $179.99 on Amazon, which is the lowest price it has reached so far. The G51F’s combination of 180Hz refresh rate, 1ms response time, and AMD FreeSync support makes fast-paced games look smoother and feel more responsive than they do on standard 60Hz displays, especially in shooters, racing games, and competitive multiplayer titles.

If you're interested in the new M5 MacBook, Amazon is the only major retailer offering a $250 discount. I’m delighted to be wrong on this one, because the entire Garmin Fenix 9 line-up is right now $100 off, the first notable discount the watch has got since it introduced in late August.

There are a lot of models to pick between in the sale, but the model I tested and use to track my own training is the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro, which is $1,099 at Amazon right now.

All models of the Garmin Fenix 9 are reduced by $100 for Black Friday, including the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro with InReach, which is the watch I tested for our review. It packs in all of Garmin's latest and greatest features, and looks great thanks to its all-titanium case.

Industry observers note that the Garmin Fenix 9 line-up includes four models. The standard Fenix 9 and three variants of the Fenix 9 Pro, all of which offer a full titanium case as a key upgrade on the base Fenix 9.

When picking between Pro models you have to decide if you want an AMOLED or MIP display — you’ll find the latter on the Fenix 9 Pro Solar.

If you want the longest battery life possible on your Fenix, then opting for a Fenix 9 Pro Solar model is the smart move. The MIP display has solar panels on it to boost the battery life in sunny conditions, and the Pro Solar will outlast the AMOLED models of the Fenix 9.

You also have to make the call on whether you want a Pro model with InReach, giving you extra connectivity when you’re in the great outdoors.

Another major decision is the size you go for — there are 43mm, 47mm and 51mm options, with the battery life and screen size growing with the case size.

All of the Fenix 9 models offers great design and outstanding sports tracking and navigation features, and they also have useful smarts like music storage with the ability to link up with streaming services.

You can still save more by opting for an older Fenix, and the Garmin Fenix 8 Pro is $849 at Amazon right now, a great deal on a watch that has Garmin’s LTE and satellite connectivity.

The Garmin Fenix 8 Pro still offers better value than the Fenix 9 in the sales thanks to this $350 saving. While the Fenix 9 Pro has a few handy updates and a more attractive all-titanium design, the older watch matches it on key features and is much cheaper.

However, if you want to get the latest model, you can now do so for $100 less, and given how new the Fenix 9 is I think any saving at all is a surprise bonus this Black Friday.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google loves a rebrand. What started off as "Spark" is now "Task" in Gemini—not to be confused with Google Tasks, the to-do app. Google took its Spark AI agent, which used to live in a separate tab, and integrated it into the Gemini interface. Gemini Task is available globally, and it’s completely free to use for some. That said, some features are limited to the U.S. and, of course, subject to some pretty strict usage limits. While not exactly a replacement for ChatGPT Dots or Meta Muse, you can think of Gemini Task as a controlled version of an AI agent that can do quite a lot in the background.

To use Task, open Gemini and create a upcoming chat. You’ll see a Task tab next to Chat. Switch to it, and start writing your prompt. (You’ll also see some suggested options here.) Type your task or action and press "Send." The feature works best if you’ve already enabled Personal Intelligence on your Google account, and have connected services like Gmail, Google Drive, and Photos as well. You can then tag “@Gmail” to use your Gmail account, or even a third-party connector. Task natively supports automation, so you can say something like, "run this task once every day," and the AI will add it to your Scheduled Tasks section.

Recent findings suggest that of course, I did the thing that every AI demo wants you to do: I asked Gemini to create a daily morning briefing for me, highlighting all important emails, calendar appointments, and tasks. And, in my experience, it works really well. It reminded me of this article's due date, that I have a couple of pitches in my inbox to review, that a credit card bill is due soon, and that there are some holidays around the corner.

Sources indicate that gemini is very good at retrieving information from emails and taking action. For example, I created an automation that collects all my coffee orders for the month and presents the data in Google Sheets. I then asked Task to create a subscription manager for me. Instead of paying for a third-party app, it took a few minutes to collate the services I pay for into one list. It even accounted for the currency differences (some subscriptions are in USD, some in INR) and gave me a tally in INR, along with things like average monthly cost, and more.

Industry observers note that while Gemini can connect to the open web, it's quite a hostile place right now for an AI bot. Websites are blocking agents from accessing their pages, which hinders their effectiveness. I asked Gemini to create a task that monitors the price of the Sony WH-1000XM5 headphones daily. For this, it asked my permission to spin up a remote browser, and loaded up Amazon, only to be blocked instantly. It did succeed in opening Croma though (a national retailer in India), but it took almost a minute for it to figure out that the price had not dropped below what I asked for. Would it be quicker and less resource-intensive if I did this myself? Yes, but the fact that Gemini can do this every evening like clockwork is the real advantage—as long as the websites comply, that is.

Recent findings suggest that if you're going to try Task in Gemini for free, there are some limitations you should know about. The free plan only lets you run tasks once per day, and you can’t be granular about the exact timing. (Paid Gemini looks have no such restrictions.) You can only run 10 tasks at the same time, while the limit is 50 tasks for AI Pro users. Compute-based usage limits will also apply, based on your plan. The free access is right now live in India, the U.S., Canada, Australia, Japan, and South Korea.

Some features, though, are only for U.S. owners. Gemini’s feature that lets you call businesses on your behalf is restricted to the States, as is the ability to forward emails to [email protected] to automatically turn the contents of the email into a task (like adding a college schedule to your calendar). U.S. users can also connect their Google Wallet account to set up payments at supported stores.

Gemini Task is not a proactive agent, nor is it trying to be. You still have to check the work. You have to approve any important steps, and if a website blocks AI models, there’s not a lot Gemini can do about it. For someone like me, who’s all-in on the Google ecosystem, I do see value in Gemini Task. The deep and robust Gmail integration is worth it alone. If you’re on the free strategy, set up a couple of background tasks related to Gmail, Google Drive, or background research that run every morning, and call it a day. And if you’re paying for AI Pro, you can get a lot more done.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ava DuVernay has been unveiled as the inaugural recipient of a upcoming London Critics’ Circle award celebrating pioneering UK film theorist Laura Mulvey, who coined the term “male gaze” in a 1970s essay.

The Laura Mulvey Female Trailblazer Award is designed to recognise the most influential women in film, who are working to break the glass ceiling, change the cultural conversation, and be an example of what is possible for future generations.

“I’ve long been interested in what happens to cinema when more kinds of people have the power to make it and have the access to watch it,” said DuVernay in response to being selected as the first recipient. Related Stories Documentary '14th' Trailer: Ava DuVernay Problems Warning About Threats To Critical Constitutional Amendment: "We Are All At Peril" Documentary Inaugural West Hollywood Human Rights Film Festival To Showcase Oscar-Contending Documentaries, 20th Anniversary Screening Of 'Blood Diamond'.

Recent findings suggest that “How much richer our understanding of the world becomes when we experience it through different voices and perspectives. Laura Mulvey’s work helped shift that conversation in profound ways, and I’m delighted to be the first recipient of an award in her name. Thank you to the LFCC. And here’s to the many women who will follow.” Watch on Deadline.

The groundbreaking director is gearing up for the theatrical release of her documentary 14th on November 27, followed by its global launch on Netflix on December 4, having world premiered at the New York Film Festival in October.

A companion piece to her 2016 documentary 13th, 14th explores the 1868 Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution and its implications for African Americans and wider equality in the U.S.

Industry observers note that duVernay’s previous credits include film work Selma, 13th, Middle of Nowhere, A Wrinkle in Time and Origin, and groundbreaking series such as When They See Us and Queen Sugar. She also the creator and driving force behind ARRAY: an arts and social impact collective dedicated to narrative change.

Widely credited with legitimising feminist film studies as an academic discipline, Mulvey is renowned not only for her films including Penthesilea: Queen of the Amazons (1974) and Riddles of the Sphinx (1977), but also for pioneering essays and books, the most famous of which is Visual Pleasure and Narrative Cinema (1975).

Mulvey coined the now ubiquitous concept of the ‘male gaze’ in the 1975 essay, in reference to the way in which women on screen would traditionally be objectified by the camera lens as a result of productions largely being controlled by men.

The academic will present the award to DuVernay at the 47th Annual London Critics’ Circle Film Awards on February 7 2026.

“In our industry, there is a plethora of women making exceptional art, but so often budgets, awards, festival line-ups and chances are still disproportionately being awarded to their male counterparts,” said Jane Crowther, Chair of the London Critics’ Circle Film Section.

“We are therefore delighted to have introduced this new special award, to honour and celebrate these women’s outstanding contributions. Just like the award’s namesake Laura Mulvey, Ava DuVernay is a true pioneer of the industry: from her exceptional filmmaking output to her extensive social impact work through ARRAY, she is a natural choice for the inaugural Female Trailblazer Award.”.

Industry observers note that this year’s ceremony will be hosted by Saturday Night Live star George Fouracres. The awards are voted for by the U.K.’s top film critics. Nominations will be announced December 18.

A forum representing four different UK regulatory bodies last month issued a warning about the potential dangers involved in using AI agents. The Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum said:.

Industry observers note that AI agents may amplify and accelerate risks and introduce fresh ones. These risks may increase as the capabilities of personal agents grow and adoption rises. Title possibly signs checks the article doesn’t have backing for. This is just a brief pro forma project patch.

It has been revealed that not much newly introduced functionality or anything to announce, last few months have mostly been bug fixes and technical debt cleanup. Most big parts of the search engine are in place, and while there are many things that could be better, we’re less likely to straight up see massive new features, at least in the immediate future. Per familiar intuition from binary searches, the closer you get to your goal the smaller and more deliberate steps you need to take in order to get even closer.

It’s been a pretty good couple of months for the project.

According to recent reports, serpApi sponsored the project with $10k a while back. Other donations and API-key sales have been going up month-over-month since this summer.

Recent findings suggest that the search engine has been working pretty well and feels like it’s going in a good direction, possibly due to a bunch of bug fixes and ongoing optimization work;I assume this is part of what’s driving up the donations. Claude also seems to have a hangup on Marginalia Search because I keep seeing it in very clearly Claude-authored search engine listicles and youtube videos. Possibly part of why it’s been getting so much attention lately? I don’t have any analytics so I really have really no idea where people are coming from, how many consumers I have, or what they’re up to.

At any rate, the operation isn’t perpetually self-sustaining yet, but number going up like it has whispers actually getting there might yet be possible.

On a related matter, I’ve been pretty slow about mailing out free API keys,you might have to wait a week or sometimes two.

I swear this isn’t because I’m nefariously trying to push people to buy a key, I’ve been getting over a dozen emails per day some days with people wanting a key, and they sometimes pile up into mountains of emails I need to reply to, and hoo boy is the process of handling these ever a bunch of manual copying of things from email to form, and then copying from form back to email again (ironically the exact sort of tedious workflow I’ve spent a good part of my career helping people streamline and automate).

Apart from fixing bugs and minor improvements, I’ve been experimenting with migrating the index code off Java to C++.

I’ve still not fully decided whether this is the direction we want to go, in general rewrites especially across language boundaries just aren’t worth it and it kinda goes against my better judgement, but we’re currently CPU bottlenecked and there might be some juice left to squeeze by skipping the JVM tax, and additionally Java really chafes for this sort of use case.

Don’t get me wrong, the newly introduced Java FFM API is miles better than anything we had before, but handling off-heap memory is still awkward and leads to a bunch of duplicated implementations or reimplementations of stuff like sorting and searching algorithms that already exists for on-heap structures but not off; bobbing in and out of native code is awkward and makes the logic difficult to follow, it just chafes.

In a recent development, should be noted the reason I’m even chasing optimizations in the index boils down to the fact that for an internet search engine, performance is recall. The search engine is only as good as the number of results it can rank within the query’s execution budget.

To be honest I’m not 100% convinced we’ll see that much performance impact, and if we do I doubt it will be massive, as the Java implementation is already very optimized, and what we’re mostly bottlenecked on isn’t the sort of places where you see substantial differences between the languages.

It has been revealed that thus far the buffer pool has been translated, and part of the main inverse index structure. These are some of the most finnicky parts of the index, and a reasonable canary for whether it’s plausible. Based on what I’ve accomplished it’s encouraging to see how much more expressive C++ is for this type of work. The vastly improved ergonomics may be a motivating factor for continuing this even if the performance doesn’t materialize.

Recent findings suggest that I’m doing this quite slowly one component at a time, measuring twice and cutting once, finding good abstractions that lean into C++’s strengths rather than doing a straight translation. In part because this is supremely fiddly and technical work, and in part because there genuinely isn’t any rush and if there is much performance to gain it’s probably in staring at the problem long enough I find better alternative approaches. I did manage to lean more into lock-free algorithms in the buffer pool for example. Translation probably won’t be finished this year at this pace.

Many things are undecided: Haven’t decided on where to draw the interface boundary yet. Neither do I have a public git repo for this. May still scrap the entire idea as a silly boondoggle. We’ll just have to see where it goes.

Sources indicate that on the off chance this rambling mess gets posted on a link aggregator somewhere, I anticipate two types of people will crawl out of the woodwork. I’ll address their concerns in advance.

Sources indicate that “Why not Rust/Zig/Odin/${MY_HOBBY_HORSE_LANGUAGE}? C++ is not memory safe! Haven’t you heard that C++ is bad? Look at this diseased rat comic I found on /r/programming!”.

It has been revealed that my friend in Christ, I use C++ because I’m experienced with C++, and have built nontrivial stuff with in in the past, I’m familiar with the tooling and also kinda enjoy it. It can not be overstated how technical this code is, it’s more than hard enough in a language I’m familiar with, let alone one I’d have to learn as I go. I don’t need to do it blindfolded using a dance mat in a barrel going down the niagara falls for this to be difficult.

"${FRONTIER_MODEL} could one-shot this in less than ${TIME}!".

According to recent reports, probably true? The source is all pretty well tested, with a reference implementation to boot. Seems like very favorable circumstances for a competent coding model.

That stated, even without turning over rocks such as “externalities of the datacenter buildout”, “externalities of AI training”, and “legal ownership status of AI-generated code”âI don’t think such angles of attack do much to convince anyone who isn’t already convincedâif AI did the translation I sure as heck couldn’t go on to then maintain that code[1][2].

Even in the best case, this is me at the edge of my programming abilities. Performance critical low level programming is hard enough to wrap your head around if you were the one who designed the code, let alone if it was vibe coded. I’d be on the hook for an AI subscription perpetually hoping and praying the token prices wouldn’t ever go up. This is a nonstarter for the same reasons the search engine runs on its own hardware and not in the cloud. You can’t be truly independent if you’re subject to the whims of a landlord.

Sources indicate that from a project management perspective, I’m not rushing anything to market. Project still has years of runway. I’m not beholden to any investors to deliver profits. Even if I wanted to, I have no employees to replace other than my self. What I would trade away is the very immersion in the problem domain that’s allowed me to get as far as I have with this project. What I’m expecting to be getting out of it is improved developer ergonomics and maybe a bit of performance if the aforementioned problem-immersion-thing pans out. That’s not something that brings me money, and something I can do because the project is in a fairly stable and mature state.

Thus, regardless of what happens in the future with AI, there isn’t an obvious opportunity cost to holding off.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

It was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes demonstrated he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward rapidly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

It has been revealed that devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n.

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

It has been revealed that you would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Recent findings suggest that top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA.

Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

According to recent reports, leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6.

Sources indicate that it was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

Sources indicate that the misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

In a recent development, decent enough watch for roughly half the game, settled on a shoot-out in which Alex Cairns got nowhere near any of Manchester United’s penalties. Doubt he will lose much sleep over it. Bruno Fernandes grinned broadly when he missed.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

Industry observers note that it’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in Upcoming Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have upcoming signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since iOS 5 in 2011, the iPhone and iPad have included Notification Center, a central place to find alerts from various apps in chronological order.
  • Starting with iOS 27, Apple is making a major change to how users open Notification Center on iPhone and iPad.
  • According to recent reports, iOS 27 is here after a summer of beta releases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since iOS 5 in 2011, the iPhone and iPad have included Notification Center, a central place to find alerts from various apps in chronological order.

Starting with iOS 27, Apple is making a major change to how users open Notification Center on iPhone and iPad.

According to recent reports, iOS 27 is here after a summer of beta releases. The behavior changed slightly between the first two releases. However, this change shipped, and I’m still adjusting to it.

In a recent development, opening Notification Center is unchanged on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 by default. However, enabling Siri AI changes a key swipe gesture on both iPhone and iPad.

Sources indicate that one of the many ways of invoking Siri AI, once enabled, is by swiping down from the center of the top edge of your iPhone or iPad display. This previously opened Notification Center.

You can still access Notification Center by swiping down from the top-left corner once Siri AI is enabled. Alerts now animate in from the top left corner. This is a way to point customers toward Notification Center’s smaller surface area.

Apple is greatly prioritizing Siri AI access in iOS 27. The majority of the top edge is devoted to invoking the latest Siri experience.

The last time Apple made a change to accessing Notification Center came when Control Center moved from a swipe up gesture from the bottom to a top-right corner swipe down gesture on iPhone X. Apple later unified this experience across devices.

In a recent development, now it’s Notification Center’s turn to be put in the corner. On iPadOS 27 beta 1 in particular, the area above Home screen app icons was pretty much devoted to invoking Siri AI. The area for opening Notification Center actually shrank if you disable displaying AM/PM or the date.

I've been always swiping from the left corner to see my notifications. I didn't even know you could swipe from the center to get to it as well 😂 I guess I'm good then?

Apple improved this with iPadOS 27 beta 2, creating a more uniform region on either side. It’s roughly the size of two app columns with Notification Center on the left and Control Center on the right. The rest is for invoking Siri.

Recent findings suggest that after 15 years of muscle memory, it’ll take some time to determine if this change is worth it or something that should be reconsidered. In the meantime, early feedback sounds overwhelmingly positive around Apple’s latest Siri AI system. Hearing that Siri is good now will also take some getting used to, I’m sure.

After months of using the newly introduced behavior, I’m certain I’d toggle it off if there were a setting to do so. Since there’s no option to disable invoking Siri from the top middle swipe down, the only thing to do is build new muscle memory around avoiding the center.

Recent findings suggest that what do you think? Would you change this back if you could? Is accessing Siri from the swipe-down gesture worth the change? Share your thoughts in the comments.

Industry observers note that PATCH, EXCLUSIVE: Slam Frank is being extended for a second time at Manhattan’s Orpheum Theatre Off Broadway. The buzzy musical will now continue an additional eight weeks through March 1, 2027.

The Andrew Fox-Joel Sinensky satirical hip-hop musical most recently extended through January 4, 2027. Both extensions are due to popular demand.

Industry observers note that PREVIOUS, NOV. 3: Slam Frank, the much talked-about Off Broadway musical that re-imagines the Anne Frank story as a multi-ethnic and genderqueer hip-hop musical, is extending its run into 2027 due to popular demand. Related Stories News Broadway's 'Two Strangers (Carry A Cake Across Upcoming York)' Announces Off Broadway Move News Barack & Michelle Obama's Higher Ground Signs On As Co-Producer Of 'Rumors' Off Broadway.

Initially set to close at the end of November, the musical by Andrew Fox and Joel Sinensky will now play through January 4, 2027, at the the Orpheum Theatre in Manhattan’s East Village. Previews began on September 17 before the official opening on October 4. Watch on Deadline.

Although the musical divided critics, it’s certainly one of the most buzzed-about Off Broadway productions of the season. The musical was inspired by a 2022 viral Twitter thread that asked, “Did Anne Frank ever acknowledge her white privilege?” Fox and Sinensky co-wrote the show drawing on actual statements from the online discourse.

Here’s the official synopsis: “Slam Frank imagines what happens when a progressive theater tech giant asks themselves that same question, transforming Anne Frank’s tragic true story into an intersectional, multi-ethnic, genderqueer, decolonized, anti-capitalist, hyper-empowering Afro-Latin hip-hop musical.” The description goes on to call the work “a satirical reckoning about identity, tribalism, and art that left audiences reeling.”.

In a recent development, directed by Sam LaFrage, choreographed by Esosa Oviasu, with music direction by Alex Harrington, Slam Frank stars Olivia Bernábe as Anita (the Anne character), Alex Lewis as Peter, Amelia Louise Barr as Margot, John Anker Bow as Mr. Van Daan, Austen Horne as Edith, Rocky Paterra as Otto, Jaz Zepatos as Mrs. Van Daan, and Walker Stovall as The Assistant Stage Manager.

The producing team includes GFour Productions, Stage Time, Steven Brandon, Andrew Fox, Alex Lewis, and Joel Sinensky, in addition to Sarah Battaglia, Erin Boeke Burke, and Katie Rosin.

Recent findings suggest that iOS 27 brought several latest features to the Messages app, including a setting that’s long been a popular request: the ability to customize or turn off the audio button. Here’s how to use it.

With iOS 27, Apple fixed a lot of bugs and also granted many feature requests from over the years.

Siri AI is the biggest example of that, offering a big upgrade over the old Siri. But smaller changes in apps like Calendar, Mail, and Messages reflect this focus on wish fulfillment.

According to recent reports, in Messages, there’s a new setting that I instantly starting using. It lets you turn off the audio button that normally lives on the right side of the text input field.

Industry observers note that the audio button has been conveniently accessible there for years, but I never use it. I don’t think I’ve ever sent an audio message. Sometimes I use dictation, but that’s always available from the bottom-right of the keyboard.

Since I never need that button, the only time it gets pressed is by accident. And as I suspect a lot of users have encountered—including Justin Bieber—it’s very easy to hit by accident.

Thankfully, iOS 27 has the fix. To disable the audio button, follow these steps:.

Even if you turn the audio button off, you can still send audio messages by hitting the + button to open your iMessage apps then selecting ‘Audio.’.

If you prefer to keep the button active, you can alternately now select ‘Record Audio’ or ‘Start Dictation’ as its function. That way the button will always stay set to your preference instead of dynamically changing like it did before.

Will you disable the audio button in Messages? Let us know in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple’s iPad lineup is incredibly strong, and two standout options are the iPad Air and iPad Pro.
  • Bonus pick: The all-newly introduced iPad mini is up to $100 off for Black Friday as well.
  • Apple updated the iPad Air earlier this year, bringing the M4 chip for improved performance along with 12GB of RAM, up from 8GB in the previous generation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple’s iPad lineup is incredibly strong, and two standout options are the iPad Air and iPad Pro. If you’re trying to decide whether the iPad Pro is worth the extra cost this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know.

Bonus pick: The all-newly introduced iPad mini is up to $100 off for Black Friday as well.

Apple updated the iPad Air earlier this year, bringing the M4 chip for improved performance along with 12GB of RAM, up from 8GB in the previous generation.

The iPad Air is available in 11-inch and 13-inch screen sizes, and uses an LCD display with a 60Hz refresh rate. This means it doesn’t offer OLED or ProMotion, unlike the iPad Pro. It uses Touch ID for biometric authentication, supports the Magic Keyboard and Apple Pencil Pro, and offers the full iPadOS multitasking experience.

The iPad Air is available in four colors: blue, purple, starlight, and space gray. It starts at 128GB of storage and can be configured up to 1TB.

According to recent reports, the iPad Pro is the best iPad money can buy. It’s powered by Apple’s M5 chip and offers many advantages over the iPad Air.

The biggest difference is the display technology. The iPad Pro is available in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes and uses Apple’s Ultra Retina XDR display with tandem OLED technology. This means it offers deeper blacks, better contrast, and higher brightness than the LCD screen found in the iPad Air.

According to recent reports, the iPad Pro also supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz. This means scrolling, animations, Apple Pencil interactions, and more will be significantly smoother.

Contrary to what the naming implies, the iPad Pro is also noticeably thinner and lighter than the iPad Air. The 11-inch iPad Pro measures 5.3mm thick, while the 13-inch model is even thinner at 5.1mm.

The iPad Pro offers Face ID instead of Touch ID, Thunderbolt connectivity, a four-speaker audio system, and nano-texture display options with the higher-end configuration.

Recent findings suggest that for most people, the iPad Air is the right choice. It delivers the entire iPad experience, excellent performance, and comes in four fun colors and two different screen sizes.

The iPad Pro is the best iPad you can buy, but it’s overkill for most people. Don’t get me wrong, I love my iPad Pro. If it’s in your holiday budget, it’s a fantastic choice. I can’t overstate how impressive the tandem OLED display is. It’s significantly better than the LCD screen on the iPad Air. It’s also great having Face ID in the iPad form factor.

The iPad Pro is slightly more tempting at its current sale price, with the mid-range 13-inch model at an impressive $350 off.

Sources indicate that still, both the iPad Air and iPad Pro run the same iPadOS experience, and that’s why I think the iPad Air is the better value for most people. What do you think? Let us know down in the comments.

#120630. Netflix As The Upcoming Cable: From Friend To Foe To Friend Again, How Streamer Became Go-To Source Of Off-Network Revenue & Tune-In Promotion

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2441 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Deadline ↗ Open Full Page

Netflix As The Upcoming Cable: From Friend To Foe To Friend Again, How Streamer Became Go-To Source Of Off-Network Revenue & Tune-In Promotion

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2441 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Deadline

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Initially welcomed by legacy media companies as an additional revenue stream for library content to offset the declines in DVD sales, third-party streamers, particularly Netflix, have evolved into a replacement for the depressed off-network syndication business and a viable promotional platform to drum up interest for fresh season rolls out on broadcast — and beyond.
  • In a recent development, the latest example is the major film and TV licensing deal Netflix recently made with Disney.
  • Disney has first-hand experience how a streaming window on Netflix can help a broadcast series via its pioneering at the time pact for ABC drama Grey’s Anatomy, which made its debut on the platform in 2015.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Initially welcomed by legacy media companies as an additional revenue stream for library content to offset the declines in DVD sales, third-party streamers, particularly Netflix, have evolved into a replacement for the depressed off-network syndication business and a viable promotional platform to drum up interest for fresh season rolls out on broadcast — and beyond.

In a recent development, the latest example is the major film and TV licensing deal Netflix recently made with Disney. It includes multi-year agreements for drama Will Trent and comedy Shifting Gears, whose existing seasons are launching on the streamer weeks ahead of their upcoming season premieres on ABC. The former debuted on Netflix earlier this month and is projected to crack the Nielsen Top 10 when the next ranking is released. Related Stories News UK Actors Union Equity To Kickstart Negotiations With Streamers Early Next Year Sports NFL Thanksgiving Week Football Schedule: How To Watch & Livestream All Games.

Disney has first-hand experience how a streaming window on Netflix can help a broadcast series via its pioneering at the time pact for ABC drama Grey’s Anatomy, which made its debut on the platform in 2015. Making previous seasons available on the streamer has recruited a new generation of fans for the medical drama, extending the series’ life on ABC where it is presently airing its 23rd season. Watch on Deadline.

The breakthrough came four years prior when the success of AMC’s Breaking Bad on Netflix helped the series avoid cancellation and become an award-winning hit for the cable network, prompting creator Vince Gilligan to give the streamer credit for keeping Breaking Bad on the air following the first of two Outstanding Drama Series Emmy wins in 2013.

Soon, there was a name for that — “the Riverdale phenomenon” — after the 2017 CW series which delivered OK, not spectacular ratings during its first season on the network before exploding on Netflix over the summer, leading to a ratings surge for the following season on the CW that fall.

“After that, everyone was like, ‘Oh, I want my show on Netflix because then everyone will watch it,'” one industry veteran recalled.

According to recent reports, still, Netflix’s output with the CW that Riverdale was part of notwithstanding, major library streaming pacts for on-air broadcast/basic cable series made after their first season were not that common, with NBC’s The Blacklist and Blindspot, Fox’s Latest Girl, Gotham and Lucifer and TNT’s Animal Kingdom as notable examples, all selling in competitive situations. (Of the six, The Blacklist, New Girl and Gotham went to Netflix, Blindspot and Lucifer were acquired by Hulu before Lucifer became a Netflix original, Animal Kingdom by Prime Video.).

NBC’s Good Girls was another streaming success story on Netflix. Licensed under an old co-production model Netflix employed in the late 2010s, its first season made its debut on Netflix in the U.S. on Jan. 1, 2019, just two months before the Season 2 launch on NBC. The series’ success on Netflix and the generous fees coming from the streamer helped keep Good Girls on the air for four seasons despite declining linear ratings.

Recent findings suggest that while lucrative for the studios, such third-party licensing agreements largely dried up when legacy media companies started launching their own streamers in 2019-20 and initially kept virtually of their series in a walled garden. That has gradually changed, with Netflix carrying more current ABC, NBC, CBS and Fox series than ever. (While Netflix has been dominating the field, there are rare exceptions with other third-party streamers, like CBS’ Ghosts being available on Prime Video.).

What has evolved from the early-days exclusive SVOD pacts is that third-party deals now are largely not exclusive: the broadcast series are available on their sibling streamers which have both in-season (next day) and out-of-season (previous seasons) rights, while Netflix and other third-party streamers get the shows out-of-season, launching a season after it has finished its broadcast run.

That is in line with how syndication worked, though the streamer is getting new broadcast series much faster than the traditional model where highlights had to make it to four seasons and 100 episodes to launch in syndication, first on local broadcast stations and then on cable.

It has been revealed that “Then cable and local markets collapsed on top of each other, and eventually streaming essentially took the place of this syndication window. But not after four years, after one year,” one industry veteran said.

Network series are now commonly sold to third-party platforms after their first season for an SVOD window that has two main entry points: a season dropping on the streamer 30 days after the season finale had been released, which shows such as Grey’s Anatomy and the the CW’s Sullivan’s Crossing adhere to on Netflix, or at the start of the next broadcast season.

The latter was the case with New Girl and The Blacklist and is right now in play with NBC comedies Happy’s Place and St. Denis Medical as well as Fox drama Doc, all on Netflix. In many cases, the fall entry point has evolved into a streaming season launch 30 or so days prior to the start of the next season on broadcast, providing an opportunity for people to get back into a show by catching up and reengaging.

That makes for strategic deployments like this fall’s Netflix premieres of ABC’s Will Trent and Shifting Gears timed to the next seasons’ debut on broadcast with a strong promotional purpose. (Will Trent dropped on Netflix two months ahead of the series’ return on ABC, for Shifting Gears, the lead-in is about 30 days.).

Fox’s Best Medicine and Animal Control — both owned by the network — also launch their previous season on Netflix a month ahead of the fresh seasons debuting on Fox.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, CBS’ Fire Country is adding a wrinkle by going back an extra season. Its first season released on Netflix about two months ahead of its Season 3 premiere on CBS in 2024, and Season 2 made its Netflix debut about two months ahead of Season 4 debut on CBS in 2025. Interestingly, Fire Country‘s presence on Netflix has been limited to these two seasons, with newer seasons only available on CBS sibling Paramount+.

One of the earliest examples of such use of Netflix after the broadcast networks already had streamers in the corporate family was a one-year non-exclusive licensing deal CBS Studios made in September 2020 to put the first seasons of drama Evil and comedy The Unicorn on Netflix ahead of the premiere of their second seasons on CBS.

Sources indicate that the stunt didn’t help the Walton Goggins comedy, which was canceled by after two seasons. (The same happened to NBC’s The Hunting Party despite a strong Season 1 launch on Netflix a little over a month into The Hunting Party‘s second season on NBC.).

In a recent development, meanwhile, Evil‘s strong sampling on Netflix helped inform the decision to move the supernatural drama from CBS to Paramount+. The series’ streaming performance also likely factored into the initial one-year non-exclusive licensing deal with Netflix getting extended to five years and the show’s first three seasons.

The way streaming releases are plotted by series’ owners is in line with the function basic cable served in its heyday for demonstrates sold in off-network syndication whose latest season would become available on cable in September, just before the next season starts airing on broadcast.

According to recent reports, to further promote a series’ return on broadcast, shows used to do marathons on cable. What is a TV marathon’s equivalent in the streaming era? Binging — or dropping the entire previous season on a platform like Netflix ahead of the new one’s network premiere.

Exposure is great but it doesn’t pay the bills — at least not directly — so the proliferation of Netflix licensing deals has been fueled by other motives too as networks and studios grapple with declines in linear ratings and the ad revenue attached to them.

It has been revealed that “There is enhanced promotion, but also economics are driving these things,” one industry insider mentioned. “Studios are carrying deficits on these reveals, they need to find revenue, so because because the four-year syndication window really is not there anymore, they have to find revenue.”.

Recent findings suggest that for studios, the latter sometimes takes precedent. “From our standpoint, we’re going to look at the money first, and then the marketing aspect second,” one studio executive noted.

The decisions are made with many factors in mind, including profit participants who get a portion of off-network revenue.

Talent agents who represent creatives have been lamenting the demise of the off-network syndication model, claiming that the money from streaming deals doesn’t come close to the syndication windfall in covering indicates’ deficits and paying profit participants, with proceeds also down from the early days of the streaming wars when Netflix was paying premium for (predominantly exclusive) SVOD rights.

Studio executives argue that money is still there for the taking, but instead of one syndication revenue stream, there are multiple steaming ones as the era of large audiences watching network demonstrates in syndication five days a week is gone. Now viewership is fractured, and so are streaming deals, non-exclusive over a myriad of platforms.

According to recent reports, “Our business is not just streaming to the big ones, Netflix and Amazon; it’s also AVOD, it’s Roku and Tubi. There’s multiple ways you can now make money, which is great,” one TV executive said. “In the aggregate for individual indicates probably will rarely get close to what a show could have made in its peak syndication days, so agents probably see that more than we do because they’re focusing on the individual performance of one show in its U.S. life cycle.”.

Exactly six years after the Riverdale phenomenon, in the summer of 2023, we had the Suits phenomenon when an old USA Network series became the biggest show in America, breaking a slew of streaming ratings records and amassing eye-popping 57.7 billion minutes watched for the year despite only launching on Netflix U.S. in June.

It showed that cable series, once thought to be of no off-network syndication value, can draw big numbers when exposed to a new, wide audience on streaming.

That carried over to pay cable too, with Starz’s biggest series, Outlander and Power, and Showtime’s signature demonstrates Dexter, Homeland, Shameless and Yellowjackets finding their way to Netflix, many of the deals driven by the series’ producing studios.

With the dire state of the linear TV business, for basic cable networks that want to stay in the original scripted programming — and some pay cable ones too — a syndication-type deal with a major streamer is a do-or-die, a crucial revenue stream that allows them to afford scripted series.

That explains the substantial newly introduced $500 million licensing deal AMC recently made with Netflix for the entire The Walking Dead universe. Ever since Breaking Bad‘s Netflix breakthrough, AMC has been licensing its biggest originals to the streamer, including The Walking Dead mothership for almost 15 years and Anne Rice’s Immortal Universe, the newer ones shared with its own platform AMC+.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Disney’s FX is essentially a streaming brand on Hulu, delivering some of the platform’s biggest hits, like American Horror Story, Love Story: John F. Kennedy Jr. & Carolyn Bessette, Shōgun, and The Bear.

In January, Netflix announced a deal with Paramount for 20 series, which, surprisingly, included a Taylor Sheridan Paramount+ original, Mayor of Kingstown.

In a recent development, HBO had previously licensed some of its originals to Netflix years after they had ended their run, including Sex and the City, Band of Brothers and Six Feet Under, with marquee series such as The Sopranos and Game of Thrones off limits. In contrast, Mayor of Kingstown is a current original on a rival streamer, part of Paramount+’s treasured Taylorverse. The other titles in the package are largely former CBS series, along with Matlock, licensed to Netflix only internationally.

According to recent reports, I hear Mayor of Kingstown was a late addition as Netflix was not willing to take the other titles without it. I hear the Mayor of Kingstown producers leveraged the series’ inclusion to get an extra season as Paramount+ had planned to end the show after Season 4. A renewal for an abbreviated fifth and final season was confirmed just days before the Netflix licensing deal, which includes the first four seasons of Mayor of Kingstown, was unveiled.

In May, David Ellison, then-CEO of Paramount, now co-CEO of Skydance, told Wall Street analysts that the firm will continue to license select programming to third parties “for the foreseeable future.”.

Amazon similarly made a Netflix deal for the first three seasons of MGM+’s acclaimed but not widely known sci-fi horror drama From, which has released four seasons and has been renewed for a fifth and final season. It has turned into a Suits/Riverdale-style phenomenon, amassing more than 5 billion minutes viewed in the U.S. in its first three weeks.

In a recent development, as part of its Netflix licensing deal, Disney took a step further by lending a top Disney+ original series in its prime, Percy Jackson and the Olympians, for an unprecedented short, three-month window, along with the Ice Age movie franchise. The stunt is timed to the release of the upcoming season of Percy Jackson on Disney+ on Nov. 20 and the new Ice Age movie, Boiling Point, on Feb. 5, 2027.

Touting the mutual benefits of the deal for Disney and Netflix, the latter’s co-CEO Ted Sarandos joked about plugging rival Disney’s Ice Age: Boiling Point on the streamer’s earnings call last month, name-checking his Disney counterpart Josh D’Amaro by quipping, “You’re welcome, Josh.”.

In a recent development, “We expect to have opportunities throughout for the best series and the best films with all the suppliers,” Sarandos mentioned about the Netflix licensing strategy. “It’s a little complicated because all of our suppliers are also our competitors. Our deals bring in much needed revenue. They certainly build awareness, and the benefit of that awareness transfers back to them because it helps grow the value of their IP. So these deals really are win-win.”.
